description: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH (ISO 15.14) - the byte-counting twin of FUNCTION LENGTH (15.50); the D7 byte-vs-position distinction. LIVE (P11 Step 7): a COMPILE-TIME FOLD (BindByteLengthFold) over DataItem.ByteWidth, which pins WiseOwl COBOL's implementor-defined per-usage byte widths (13.18.60 leaves them to the implementor): DISPLAY/BIT 1 byte per position, NATIONAL 2 bytes per position (UTF-16), BINARY/PACKED/BINARY-CHAR..DOUBLE the StorageWidth, float 4/8, index/pointer/object-reference 8. Runtime-length shapes (ref-mod/ODO/ANY LENGTH) stay loud by name. A COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 text with its Intrinsic Function amendment (X3.23a-1989) has functions of three types only, §1989:A.2.3: "Data item functions are elementary data items and return alphanumeric, numeric, or integer values", and its Table 1 (§1989:A.2.4: "Table 1 on pages A-30 through A-32 summarizes the functions that are available") lists ACOS through UPPER-CASE, LENGTH among them and no BYTE-LENGTH; §2002:15.12 adds "The BYTE-LENGTH function returns an integer equal to the length of the argument in bytes", and §2002:F.2 item 78 ("New intrinsic functions are") lists BYTE-LENGTH (item 77: "Previously, the intrinsic function facility was a separate module and its implementation was optional"). §2014:15.13 and §2023:15.14.1 carry the 2002 sentence unchanged (vs §2023:15.50.1: "The LENGTH function returns an integer equal to the length of the argument in alphanumeric character positions" ...). Below 2002 the D8 catalog window rejects by name+edition (COBOL1502).
vcr: 2002 introduction (§2002:F.2 item 78; the M2 catalog BYTE-LENGTH)
